metadata.description: Channelization and technology metadata for US spectrum 30 MHz-6 GHz, linked to us_allocations_30MHz_6GHz rows by frequency overlap.

allocation_source.source: FCC Online Table of Frequency Allocations (47 C.F.R. § 2.106), Office of Engineering and Technology
allocation_source.source_revision: Revised on July 1, 2022 (as printed on the PDF cover page)
allocation_source.secondary_source_revision: Revised on February 1, 2021 (Word edition; used only for edge consistency check)

metadata.conventions: Frequencies in MHz unless a field name says khz. Fields set to null were not confirmed against the cited source; unverified_fields names values that are quoted but not re-checked. Lists of 3GPP channel bandwidths are the commonly supported sets and are not exhaustive per release.

technologies.name: FM broadcast
technologies.modulation: Wideband FM, ±75 kHz peak deviation (100% modulation); 19 kHz stereo pilot with 38 kHz DSB-SC L-R subcarrier; optional 57 kHz RBDS subcarrier; optional HD Radio (IBOC) digital sidebands
sources: 47 CFR 73.201 (numerical designation of FM broadcast channels)
technologies.notes: Channel 200 (87.9 MHz) is limited to Class D stations by 73.512.

technologies.name: Television broadcast (ATSC 1.0 / ATSC 3.0)

channel_plan.channel_37_608_614_mhz: not assigned to TV (radio astronomy / WMTS)
channel_plan.repack_completion: Incentive Auction transition (channels 38-51 cleared for 600 MHz wireless) completed 13 July 2020

modulation.atsc_1_0: 8-VSB, 10.762 Msymbol/s, pilot 309.441 kHz above lower channel edge, 19.39 Mbit/s (ATSC A/53)
modulation.atsc_3_0: COFDM (8K/16K/32K FFT), LDPC/BCH, 6 MHz channel (ATSC A/322)

sources: FCC Incentive Auction Task Force, transition schedule (repack completed July 2020)
technologies.notes: Channels 14-20 (470-512 MHz) are shared with Part 90 land mobile in eleven metropolitan areas (T-band).

technologies.name: Private land mobile, VHF low band (Part 90)
technologies.modulation: Analog FM (20K0F3E) predominantly
sources: 47 CFR 90.20 (Public Safety Pool frequency table, 20 kHz increments in 25-50 MHz)

technologies.name: Private land mobile, VHF high band (Part 90)
technologies.modulation: Analog FM 11K2F3E (12.5 kHz) or digital P25 / DMR / NXDN (see separate entries); 25 kHz operation prohibited since 1 Jan 2013 (narrowbanding)
sources: 47 CFR 90.20(c)(3) and 90.35(b)(3) (frequency tables, 7.5 kHz channel steps 150.8-162 MHz)
47 CFR 90.209(b)(5) (authorized bandwidth 150-174 MHz: 11.25 kHz, 20 kHz for legacy licensees until 2013 deadline)
47 CFR 90.203(j) (narrowbanding: 12.5 kHz or equivalent efficiency required after 1 January 2013)
technologies.notes: Federal land mobile in the same range (162.0375-174 MHz federal FIXED/MOBILE) follows NTIA Manual Chapter 4 channel plans, not Part 90.

technologies.name: Private land mobile, UHF 450-470 MHz and T-band 470-512 MHz (Part 90)

bands.note: T-band; 11 metropolitan areas only, shared with TV channels 14-20

technologies.modulation: Analog FM 11K2F3E or digital P25 / DMR / NXDN; 6.25 kHz channels (NXDN, dPMR) also authorized
sources: 47 CFR 90.20 and 90.35 (frequency tables, 6.25 kHz steps 450-470 MHz)

technologies.name: 220-222 MHz land mobile (Part 90 Subpart T)
technologies.modulation: Narrowband (ACSB / linear modulation, digital)
sources: 47 CFR 90.715 (220-222 MHz channel table: 5 kHz channel pairs)

technologies.name: 700 MHz public safety narrowband and broadband
technologies.modulation: P25 Phase 1/2 on narrowband channels; LTE band 14 on broadband segment
sources: 47 CFR 90.531 (700 MHz public safety band plan; 6.25 kHz narrowband channels)

technologies.name: 800 MHz land mobile (806-824 / 851-869 MHz)
technologies.modulation: Analog FM (20K0F3E), P25, and ESMR (iDEN historically; now LTE band 26 in the 817-824/862-869 ESMR segment)
sources: 47 CFR 90.614 (800 MHz band segments after rebanding)
technologies.notes: NPSPAC public safety channels (806-809/851-854 MHz) use 12.5 kHz offsets from the 25 kHz grid.
unverified_fields: channel_raster_khz (25 kHz base grid per 90.613; interleaved 12.5 kHz offsets exist in NPSPAC)

technologies.name: 900 MHz land mobile and 900 MHz broadband segment (896-901 / 935-940 MHz)
technologies.modulation: Narrowband FM/digital on 12.5 kHz channels; 3 MHz x 3 MHz broadband segment (897.5-900.5 / 936.5-939.5 MHz) authorized 2020 for LTE (3GPP band 8 covers this range)
sources: FCC 20-67, Report and Order, WT Docket 17-200 (900 MHz broadband segment, May 2020)

technologies.name: APCO Project 25 (P25) digital land mobile

modulation.phase_1: C4FM (4-level FSK), 4800 symbols/s, 9600 bit/s, 12.5 kHz channel; CQPSK receive-compatible variant
modulation.phase_2: 2-slot TDMA in 12.5 kHz (6.25 kHz equivalent), 12 kbit/s; H-DQPSK outbound, H-CPM inbound

sources: TIA-102.BBAB / TIA-102.BBAC (P25 Phase 2 two-slot TDMA physical layer / MAC)
technologies.notes: Band list gives ranges where P25 systems are commonly licensed; the waveform itself is band-agnostic.

technologies.name: DMR (ETSI Digital Mobile Radio)
technologies.modulation: 4FSK, 4800 symbols/s, 9600 bit/s, 2-slot TDMA (30 ms slots, 60 ms frame) in 12.5 kHz

technologies.name: NXDN digital land mobile
technologies.modulation: 4FSK FDMA; 2400 symbols/s (4800 bit/s) in 6.25 kHz or 4800 symbols/s (9600 bit/s) in 12.5 kHz
sources: NXDN Technical Specifications, Part 1-A Common Air Interface (NXDN Forum)

technologies.name: Analog FM land mobile voice
technologies.modulation: FM voice; emission designators 11K2F3E (±2.5 kHz deviation, 12.5 kHz channel), 16K0F3E (±5 kHz, 25 kHz channel), 20K0F3E (VHF low band / 800 MHz); CTCSS (67-254 Hz) and DCS squelch subaudible signalling

technologies.name: GMRS / FRS (Part 95 Subparts E and B)
technologies.modulation: FM; FRS 12.5 kHz (11K2F3E), GMRS 20 kHz (16K0F3E) on main channels and 12.5 kHz on interstitial channels

technologies.name: MURS (Part 95 Subpart J)
technologies.modulation: FM (or other) within 11.25 or 20 kHz, 2 W ERP

technologies.name: VHF aeronautical mobile (R) voice (air band)

channel_plan.icao_8_33_khz_spacing: defined in ICAO Annex 10 Vol V (2280 channels); implemented in European airspace; not the operating channel plan in US domestic airspace as of the source date

technologies.modulation: AM double-sideband voice (A3E), 6K00A3E; ACARS data 2400 bit/s MSK on AM (131.550 MHz primary US); VDL Mode 2 D8PSK 31.5 kbit/s (136.975 MHz common signalling channel)
sources: 47 CFR 87.173 (frequencies available: 25 kHz spaced channels 118.000-136.975 MHz)
ICAO Annex 10 Volume III Part II (VHF voice, 25 kHz / 8.33 kHz channel spacing)
ICAO Annex 10 Volume V (frequency utilization, 8.33 kHz plan)
ICAO Annex 10 Volume III Part I Chapter 6 (VDL Mode 2)
technologies.notes: Aeronautical mobile (R) 136-137 MHz is used for data link (VDL) in the US.
unverified_fields: icao_8_33_khz_spacing US status (regulatory statement not verified in a primary US document)

technologies.name: VOR, ILS localizer, ILS glide slope, marker beacon

channel_plan.vor_mhz: 108.00-117.95 MHz in 50 kHz steps; 108.0-111.95 even-tenth (x.x0, x.x5 with even first decimal) channels for VOR, odd-tenth for localizer
channel_plan.glide_slope_mhz: 329.15-335.00 MHz, 40 channels, 150 kHz spacing, paired to localizer channel

technologies.modulation: VOR: AM with 30 Hz reference/variable phase, 9960 Hz FM subcarrier, 1020 Hz ident; localizer/glide slope: 90/150 Hz AM modulation depth difference; marker: A2E 400/1300/3000 Hz tones
sources: ICAO Annex 10 Volume I, Chapter 3.1 (ILS), 3.3 (VOR), 3.1.7 (marker beacons)

technologies.name: DME / TACAN

channel_plan.reply_offset_mhz: reply = interrogation ± 63 MHz (X: -63 for N<=63, +63 for N>63; Y: opposite sense)

technologies.modulation: Gaussian pulse pairs, pulse-position (interrogate/reply), ~2700 pulse-pairs/s transponder; TACAN adds 15 Hz / 135 Hz bearing modulation

technologies.name: SSR / Mode S / ADS-B 1090ES / TCAS

modulation.1030_uplink: Mode A/C: P1/P2/P3 0.8 µs pulses (8 µs / 21 µs spacing); Mode S: 2 preamble pulses + DPSK 4 Mbit/s data block (56 or 112 bits)
modulation.1090_downlink: Mode A/C: 0.45 µs pulses, 12 pulse frame (20.3 µs); Mode S / ADS-B extended squitter: 8 µs preamble + PPM 1 Mbit/s, 56/112-bit messages (120 µs)

sources: ICAO Annex 10 Volume IV (Surveillance radar and collision avoidance systems), Chapter 3
RTCA DO-260B / EUROCAE ED-102A (1090 MHz Extended Squitter MOPS)
47 CFR 87.187 (frequencies for aircraft stations: 1030/1090 MHz transponders)
technologies.notes: UAT (978 MHz) listed separately.

technologies.name: UAT ADS-B (978 MHz)
technologies.modulation: Continuous-phase binary FSK, 1.041667 Mbit/s, ±312.5 kHz deviation; 1 s frame with ground uplink segment (188 ms) and ADS-B segment (32 message start opportunities per ms)
unverified_fields: channel_bandwidth_khz (occupied bandwidth figure not confirmed against DO-282B)

technologies.name: Emergency beacons (ELT/EPIRB/PLB) 406 MHz and 121.5 MHz homing

channel_plan.406_channels_mhz: 406.025-406.076 MHz, 3 kHz channel spacing, assigned by Cospas-Sarsat channel plan

technologies.modulation: 406 MHz: 5 W, biphase-L PSK ±1.1 rad, 400 bit/s, 112/144-bit burst every ~50 s; 121.5 MHz: AM swept tone (A3X) low power homing
